title: PMDformer: Patch-Mean Decoupling Information Transformer for Long-term Forecasting
claim: Subtracting each patch's mean makes attention reflect true shape similarity, and the resulting model beats all baselines across every benchmark dataset.
layout: 3 parts, left-to-right: stacked before/after time-series patches, stacked before/after attention heatmaps with colorbar, and a radar chart comparing methods on 5 datasets
description: The figure has three zones. On the left, two stacked line plots show a long time series split into three colored patches (P1 blue, P2 magenta, P3 orange). The top plot is the original sequence, with dashed per-patch mean lines at different levels. The bottom plot shows the same patches after mean subtraction, centered on zero, with dashed vertical separators. In the middle, two 3x3 attention-weight heatmaps (Before on top, After below) show numeric values in blue shades, with a shared vertical colorbar. A few After values are highlighted in red, green and blue. On the right, a radar chart covers five datasets (ETT, Solar, Traffic, Weather, ECL). A large red pentagon for PMDformer encloses the other methods' smaller colored polygons. Red numbers mark its MSE at each axis, and a legend sits at the bottom. The eye goes first to the red pentagon.
caption: Comparison of the MSE of all baselines with our proposed PMDformer. The results are the averages for all prediction lengths.
abstract: Long-term time series forecasting (LTSF) plays a crucial role in fields such as energy management, finance, and traffic prediction. Transformer-based models have adopted patch-based strategies to capture long-range dependencies, but accurately modeling shape similarities across patches and variables remains challenging due to scale differences. To address this, we introduce patch-mean decoupling (PMD), which separates the trend and residual shape information by subtracting the mean of each patch, preserving the original structure and ensuring that the attention mechanism captures true shape similarities. Futhermore, to more effectively model long-range dependencies and capture cross-variable relationships, we propose Trend Restoration Attention (TRA) and Proximal Variable Attention (PVA). The former module reintegrates the decoupled trend from PMD while calculating attention output. And the latter focuses cross-variable attention on the most relevant, recent time segments to avoid overfitting on outdated correlations. Combining these components, we propose PMDformer, a model designed to effectively capture shape similarity in long-term forecasting scenarios. Extensive experiments indicate that PMDformer outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in stability and accuracy across multiple LTSF benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/aohu1105/PMDformer.
